content: This overlaps with a master's thesis I'm supervising: @Hannah Scholz is working on precisely this topic, aiming for mathlib inclusion (and without AI use, as I understand is currently required by university regulations).
I just registered this as a project intention: https://github.com/leanprover-community/project-intentions/issues/32 I'm sorry for not doing so earlier.

In terms of mathematics:

  • the inverse function theorem belongs into mathlib (and there is an open PR adding a basic version)
  • we also looked at Hirsch's proof for the project; the associated globalization theorem has hypotheses which Hirsch does not explicitly verify. (I'm cautiously optimistic they are satisfied here, though.)
  • integral curves also make sense for interior points; their existence is just not proven for boundary points yet. That's simply a gap to fill.
With my moderator's hat on: did you use AI to write your message? Note that using AI to write comments on Zulip is not allowed (per #community-guidelines; that's a link).

Some thoughts on situations like this:

For the corresponding piece of math to be well treated as they deserve, it's always better to have human dedicated formalization work in Mathlib (or standalone but reusable formalization projects), where the formalization process enriches the understanding and resonates with other branches of math.

If I understand the distinctions here correctly, Tau Ceti is where contributors fill in gaps with agents, when human dedicated efforts are temporarily absent, to have prelimilary concensurs on the reusable math APIs and formalization paths, for their (potential) dedicated consumer projects.

Utensil Song said:

If I understand the distinctions here correctly, Tau Ceti is where contributors fill in gaps with agents, when human dedicated efforts are temporarily absent, to have prelimilary concensurs on the reusable math APIs and formalization paths, for their (potential) dedicated consumer projects.

... except that it's unclear how much consensus actually forms, how much insight is gained through in Tau Ceti. Nobody knows yet. (Indeed, some obstacles you only realize by proceeding further; I don't know if AI will notice "there's something wrong here" or just paper over that.)

My working theory is that publicly accessible frontier model will saturate at some point and set that ceiling as a baseline for human to work from there. No one gets anything right the first time, so the first few times could be by agents. However, human should actively engage and inspect in the process, otherwise nothing could be learned for the do-over.

Experiences with agents suggest that they will miss important things obviously to human, treat them as elephant in the room, and happy to proceed on the narrow task in tunnel vision without flagging issues. Rounds of reviews and audits by agents could still converge without noticing them. We just have to open the box to spot the new variants.

Yes, we need to update the roadmaps here to fill the gap. @Michael Rothgang and/or @Hannah Scholz would you prefer that no one else works on this, even in Tau Ceti form, in the meantime? Or is it okay if an independent Tau Ceti level implementation lands while you are working on your version?
Good question. I'll discuss with Hannah (this is not just my decision to make).
Hi, thanks for asking! Would it be okay if I tell you my answer tomorrow after I have a chance to discuss this with Michael in person?

Moderation note: I have deleted the initial comment to this thread, as it was AI-written. Some key points it mentioned were

  • asking about the status of the Collar neighbourhood theorem (which is on the geometric topology roadmap)
  • discussion two potential proofs (Lee's and Hirsch's textbooks),
  • asking about the status of the (manifold) inverse function theorem, which is missing from mathlib.

Please use your own words to discuss here. AI-generated comments will be deleted and the poster suspended.

@Michael Rothgang, I think that was incorrect, and would prefer that good faith first time posters receive an explanation about the necessity of writing in their own words, and making sure to clearly preface or quote any LLM generated text, before anyone deletes posts or talks about suspensions.

If the post is nonsense, or crackpot, or even just not at all interesting, then fine, of course junk on sight. But none of those applied here.

Kim, thanks for calling me out; it's good to discuss. I hear what you're saying (but disagree in this case). Note that,

  • the user received such an explanation via the Zulip welcome message (even mentioning this requirement to use own words explicitly), and
  • I asked them explicitly upthread whether they used AI (and their response was AI-generated and did not engage with this at all)

so the policy you're talking about does not quite apply here.

(I also somewhat disagree that you're describing existing moderation policy - but that's a discussion for the mods. I'll take it there.)

Michael Rothgang said:

Good question. I'll discuss with Hannah (this is not just my decision to make).

Hannah and I have talked about this in person. At the moment, we prefer for Tau Ceti development to wait on this project being completed. (This will take in the order of three months; upstreaming to mathlib is happening during the projet already, so will hopefully not take much longer. Everybody is welcome to help by reviewing PRs.)

Kim Morrison said:

think that was incorrect, and would prefer that good faith first time posters receive an explanation about the necessity of writing in their own words, and making sure to clearly preface or quote any LLM generated text, before anyone deletes posts or talks about suspensions.

Sorry I am quite confused here. Isn't this exactly what done in this case? Certainly we should expect messages pointing at policies where the rationale is documented to count as such an explanation. I think this already above and beyond in terms of guidance.

@Michael Rothgang, just noting there's a question about the project-intentions registration for collar neighbourhoods that needs your or Hannah's response: https://github.com/leanprover-community/project-intentions/issues/32#issuecomment-5346152106

I've recorded the request for Tau Ceti to not work on this intention at https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/issues/285. (Note that there's no global mechanism for Tau Ceti to read project-intentions. This one is more or less a guinea pig to work out what shape, if any, that should take.)

Thanks for the reminder - replied on the intentions issue. For the request, I don't see why this mentions differential geometry elaborators (as these are not part of the roadmap, I believe). Who knows how the agents would deal with this?
